guidance.heading: 2026 Guidance
section: The Company’s estimates for net income attributable to common stockholders per diluted share and Real Estate FFO per diluted share for the year ending December 31, 2026 are included in the table below and are reconciled in the Company’s supplemental information. The Company is increasing its outlook for full year 2026 Real Estate FFO per diluted share to $13.30 to $13.40, an increase of $0.10 per diluted share from previous estimates.

desk.headline: Real Estate FFO up 4.7% to $3.37 a share, beat; full-year FFO outlook raised above estimates and dividend lifted

numbers.eps_basis: adjusted (Real Estate FFO per diluted share)

other.label: Retailer sales per sq ft (12 months)

results: Real Estate FFO, the key REIT profit measure, rose 4.7% to $3.37 a share; GAAP EPS fell to $1.54 because of $0.27 of non-cash mark-to-market losses.
Total revenue rose 13% to $1.81bn; domestic property NOI grew 6.6%.
Occupancy rose to 96.5%, base rent rose 6.1% to $62.75 per sq ft and tenants' sales per sq ft rose 14.8% to $852.
The quarterly dividend goes up to $2.30 (+4.5% y/y); Simon bought back 1.14m shares for $236.5m in the quarter.
Liquidity stood at about $9.0bn after $800m of new senior notes and $970m of secured loans.

guidance.summary: Simon raised its 2026 Real Estate FFO outlook by $0.10 to $13.30–13.40 a share, above the $13.24 analysts expected. Its GAAP EPS range was cut to $6.32–6.42.

points: Leasing stays strong: about 1,200 leases signed in Q3, rents on new deals up 17% this year with lower tenant allowances, and a pipeline up 30%.
October shopper traffic matched Q3's mid-3% growth, and retailers are upbeat about the holiday season.
Higher interest costs will be a similar ~$0.30 a share headwind in 2027; full 2027 guidance comes in February.
Simon agreed to buy University Village in Seattle, expected to close in Q4, and has a $1.2bn development pipeline at a 9% yield.
Buybacks will be done selectively, not "just do it to do it".
call.source: Earnings call transcript — The Motley Fool, 6 Nov 2026

watch: Holiday-season retailer sales and traffic, which management says shape the 2027 view.
2027 guidance in February, including the interest-cost headwind.
Further non-cash swings from the Klépierre exchangeable bonds hitting GAAP earnings.
